hotspots.topic: Fire Marshal authority and plan review
hotspots.whyItMatters: Understand where the State Fire Marshal's authority sits relative to the local AHJ for fire-protection-related electrical work (alarms, sign structures near assembly occupancies, etc.).
hotspots.cite: F.S. 633 (see the Manual's Fire Marshal chapter)
hotspots.trap: Assuming a local building inspector's sign-off automatically satisfies a State Fire Marshal review trigger.

hotspots.whyItMatters: Mounting heights and accessible-route rules intersect directly with electrical rough-in — switch/receptacle heights, panel clearances, reach range.
hotspots.cite: ADA Title III, 42 U.S.C. 12181 et seq.; F.S. 553 (Florida Accessibility Code) — see the Manual's ADA chapter
hotspots.trap: Carrying a residential mounting-height habit onto a commercial job, where the accessible reach-range rule actually governs.

hotspots.whyItMatters: What a licensed contractor must retain (contracts, permits, financial records) and for how long, tested as straight business-law recall.
hotspots.cite: F.S. 489 — see the Manual's recordkeeping chapter
hotspots.trap: Assuming project records can be discarded once a job passes final inspection — retention duties usually outlast the job itself.

hotspots.whyItMatters: Notice-to-owner and claim-of-lien timing is some of the most heavily tested business-law material in the whole exam.
hotspots.cite: F.S. 713, Part I — see the Manual's liens chapter
hotspots.trap: Missing the notice-to-owner deadline and assuming lien rights survive automatically without it.

hotspots.whyItMatters: Coverage requirements and exemptions for contractors and their employees/subcontractors.
hotspots.cite: F.S. 440 — see the Manual's workers' compensation chapter
hotspots.trap: Assuming a signed exemption for the general contractor also exempts every subcontractor working on the job.

hotspots.topic: Tax and labor law (sales tax / FLSA)
hotspots.whyItMatters: Combines Florida sales/use tax basics for contractors with federal wage-and-hour (overtime) rules — two different bodies of law tested together.
hotspots.cite: F.S. 212; Fair Labor Standards Act, 29 U.S.C. 201 et seq. — see the Manual's tax/labor chapter
hotspots.trap: Assuming a flat-rate or lump-sum contract removes the tax obligation on materials, or treating every worker as overtime-exempt by job title alone.
